instruction:
Installed tools: LibreCAD: `/usr/bin/librecad`; FreeCAD: `/usr/bin/freecad`; KiCad: `/home/user/Applications/kicad-10.0.2/kicad-10.0.2-x86_64.AppImage`; Blender: `/home/user/Applications/blender-4.2.3-linux-x64/blender`. Required four-software transfer workflow: LibreCAD -> FreeCAD -> KiCad -> Blender. Start from the provided seed DXF /home/user/Desktop/seed_motor_driver_heatsink_carrier.dxf; do not start from a blank or unrelated drawing. Run the stages in order. Each stage must read the preceding stage output, and every required intermediate file must be saved on the Desktop. The design token for this task is EW4G03; keep this token visible in the DXF labels and KiCad silkscreen. The Blender output must visibly consume the stage-2 STL and stage-3 SVG through Blender's native import/export operations.

Design goal: Motor driver carrier plate with heatsink and terminal zones. This case is intentionally different from the other benchmark cases: domain=power_electronics_mount, mechanical target=a power carrier assembly with visible heatsink fins and blue terminal blocks, electronics target=a motor-driver PCB with MOSFETs, two motor outputs, VIN terminal, and heatsink keepout.

1. LibreCAD stage: open the provided seed file /home/user/Desktop/seed_motor_driver_heatsink_carrier.dxf in LibreCAD, use it as the starting drawing, complete the required 2D geometry, remove all GUIDE construction entities, and save /home/user/Desktop/stage1_motor_driver_heatsink_carrier.dxf. Use millimeters. Use layers OUTLINE, SLOT, HOLE, LABEL. On SLOT, draw exactly three nondegenerate closed polyline zones (two separated terminal zones and one larger central heatsink zone) and exactly seven spatially distinct, mutually parallel straight fin-guide lines associated with the central zone. The overall drawing envelope must be 125 mm x 78 mm. Include the required circular features: center (10,10) radius 2.4; center (115,10) radius 2.4; center (10,68) radius 2.4; center (115,68) radius 2.4; center (62.5,39) radius 3. Add readable labels EW4G03, MOTOR-A, MOTOR-B, VIN on the LABEL layer.
2. FreeCAD stage: import /home/user/Desktop/stage1_motor_driver_heatsink_carrier.dxf in FreeCAD. Create the 3D mechanical body from that LibreCAD DXF, and export the body as /home/user/Desktop/stage2_motor_driver_heatsink_carrier.stl with an approximate bounding size of 125 mm x 78 mm x 16 mm. Then, from the same FreeCAD model, export a top-face or board-interface outline for KiCad as /home/user/Desktop/stage2_motor_driver_heatsink_carrier_handoff_outline.dxf. This handoff DXF must represent the same XY envelope as the FreeCAD body, carry all five stage-1 interface holes, and export the visible labels FREECAD_TO_KICAD and EW4G03 as two FreeCAD ShapeString outline objects.
3. KiCad stage: open KiCad and use /home/user/Desktop/stage2_motor_driver_heatsink_carrier_handoff_outline.dxf as the geometric source for a matching 125 mm x 78 mm rectangular Edge.Cuts outline; importing the DXF or accurately recreating its four outline segments are equivalent. Save /home/user/Desktop/stage3_motor_driver_heatsink_carrier_board.kicad_pcb. Add five native footprints: Q1 and Q2 as four-pad power MOSFETs, J1 and J2 as three-pad motor outputs, and J3 as a two-pad VIN terminal. Add a native Dwgs.User heatsink keepout rectangle from (40,22) to (85,56). Add F.SilkS text carrying KICAD_TO_BLENDER, EDGE_FROM_STAGE2_HANDOFF, the stage2 handoff filename, EW4G03, MOSFET-Q1, MOSFET-Q2, MOTOR-A-J1, MOTOR-B-J2, VIN-J3, and HEATSINK-KEEP. Then use KiCad's plot/export workflow to create /home/user/Desktop/stage3_motor_driver_heatsink_carrier_board_profile.svg from the same Edge.Cuts outline.
4. Blender stage: open Blender. Import /home/user/Desktop/stage2_motor_driver_heatsink_carrier.stl with Blender's STL importer, then import /home/user/Desktop/stage3_motor_driver_heatsink_carrier_board_profile.svg with Blender's SVG importer. Correct the SVG import scale so its visible profile matches the full 125 mm x 78 mm carrier. Keep the imported STL body and SVG-derived profile geometry in the scene. Make the assembled visualization visibly contain seven heatsink fins, two distinct MOSFET modules, and three distinct blue terminal blocks for MOTOR-A, MOTOR-B, and VIN; simple manufactured-looking geometry is acceptable. Export glTF Binary (.glb) as /home/user/Desktop/stage4_motor_driver_heatsink_carrier.glb. Do not satisfy these requirements with names or manually injected metadata alone.

Required deliverables on the Desktop: /home/user/Desktop/stage1_motor_driver_heatsink_carrier.dxf, /home/user/Desktop/stage2_motor_driver_heatsink_carrier.stl, /home/user/Desktop/stage2_motor_driver_heatsink_carrier_handoff_outline.dxf, /home/user/Desktop/stage3_motor_driver_heatsink_carrier_board.kicad_pcb, /home/user/Desktop/stage3_motor_driver_heatsink_carrier_board_profile.svg, /home/user/Desktop/stage4_motor_driver_heatsink_carrier.glb.

[Software] Use LibreCAD first, then FreeCAD, then KiCad, then Blender. Do not skip stages, reorder stages, or recreate the final result in only one software package.
